The education system requires fundamental reimagining. Current methods date to the industrial revolution. We train students for a world that no longer exists, teaching them to follow instructions and memorize facts.

Critical thinking, creativity, adaptability - these skills matter most in our rapidly changing world. Yet standardized testing and rigid curricula prioritize conformity over innovation. Students learn to produce correct answers rather than ask meaningful questions.

I propose a different approach. Project-based learning. Real-world problems. Interdisciplinary collaboration. Let students grapple with complexity, make mistakes, develop solutions. This builds resilience and genuine understanding. Knowledge divorced from application is mere trivia. Education should prepare people for life, not just employment.
